solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tiny amount from bank one dumped in vehicle

indicators.note: something dumped in a vehicle ends up sitting inside it

blocks.note: BK is the abbreviation for bank

explanation.surface: A bank teller sneaks a tiny sum out by dumping it in a getaway van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' tempts a solver towards a river or a lender, but here it is only its two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubkis is American slang, from Yiddish, for nothing at all or a trifling quantity.

clue.text: Boats about to go into harbour banks?

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: sandbars are banks lying across a harbour mouth

explanation.surface: Small craft are about to head into port by the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that harbour banks are the sandbars across a harbour entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A barca is a type of small boat, a word from Spanish and Italian.

clue.text: Old historian on island, fellow who would pray

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece on another sits above it

explanation.surface: An ancient chronicler on an island, a devout man at his prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedeman was one paid to pray for the souls of others, such as a benefactor.

clue.text: Arranger of festival in Cheshire town on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen in writing

blocks.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A broadcast about someone organising a carnival in a north-west English town.
explanation.definitionFit: A krewe is one of the clubs that stage parades and balls at the New Orleans Mardi Gras.

clue.text: Go away — explosive will bring blast!

explanation.surface: A frantic warning to clear off before the bomb goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathe is an old verb meaning to harm or injure, as blast does when used of withering or destroying.

clue.text: Navy game reveals gullible person, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

explanation.surface: A sailors' pastime exposes which shipmate is easily taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the S of SUCKER to the back gives UCKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Uckers is a board game like ludo traditionally played in the Royal Navy.

clue.text: It's day care arranged for female supporters

indicators.note: arranged letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Childcare has been organised for working mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' suggests backers or fans; here it is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: Caryatids are columns carved as draped women that hold up an entablature.

clue.text: Skeleton keys abandoned not stolen, surprisingly found in plant (dubiously!)

indicators.note: not means the following word is left out
abandoned suggests wild disorder, the letters thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Discarded skeleton keys, not taken by burglars, turn up in a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the letters of STOLEN from SKELETON KEYS leaves K, E, K, E, Y, S to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Keksye is a doubtful Shakespearean form of kex, a dry hollow-stemmed umbelliferous plant.

clue.text: French ranks, say, standing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means reading from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: French soldiers in their lines, rising to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Les états are the French estates, the social orders or ranks of the ancien régime.

clue.text: Fish is appetizing, not very old

indicators.note: not means the following abbreviation is left out

blocks.note: V for very, O for old

explanation.surface: A fish dish is tasty, and quite fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: VO comes out of SAVOURY.
explanation.definitionFit: The saury is a long-beaked marine fish, also called the skipper.

clue.text: What could make ape itchier are clusters of leaves

indicators.note: the letters are remade into something else, as if built from scratch

blocks.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

explanation.surface: A question about what would make a monkey even more itchy, perhaps nettles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' looks like the verb linking to the definition, but it is the unit of area supplying the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Perichaetia are the clusters of modified leaves surrounding the reproductive organs of mosses.

clue.text: Wild vegetable finally discovered in country, growing in rubbish

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words that follow and precede it
wild suggests letters running out of control into a new order
the pair of letters is placed within the word for country

explanation.surface: A wild plant found out in the countryside, sprouting among rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' serves both vegetable and discovered; 'country' is the adjective, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruderal is the botanical term for plants that colonise waste ground and rubbish heaps.

clue.text: Back at ease in the cop shop again?

explanation.surface: Relaxing once more in the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: someone back in the police station has been taken in again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rearrested has been detained by police a second time, so is back at the station.

clue.text: Old riddle making one crease up

indicators.note: made up suggests a fresh composition, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient puzzle so funny it makes someone fold up laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' is not a puzzle here but a coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Searce is an archaic word for a sieve, and a riddle is a large sieve for soil or grain.

clue.text: Revolutionary given to drinking becomes chatterer as before

blocks.note: wet can mean boozy or not in favour of prohibition

explanation.surface: A revolutionary who takes to the bottle turns into a bore, just as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks the definition as an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewet is an old word for a chattering person, originally a jackdaw.

clue.text: Secretive person no longer hearing — good person locked in

indicators.note: something locked in is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: oyer is an archaic legal word for a hearing, as in oyer and terminer

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped person, now deaf, keeps a good man shut away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks an archaic word, here the legal term from the old English courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone as close as an oyster keeps everything shut inside, so the word names a very uncommunicative person.

clue.text: Queen maybe eats Indian food, avoiding extremes — it's delicately flavoured

indicators.note: dropping both ends of a word removes its extremes
what is eaten ends up inside the eater

blocks.note: CURRY without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Her Majesty tucks into a curry, but a mild one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' points at royalty, but the queen here is an insect from the hive.
explanation.definitionFit: A beurré is a soft, buttery-fleshed variety of pear with a delicate taste.

clue.text: Refusal, for example, to continue after any changes

indicators.note: the word any changes its letter order
one piece follows on behind the other

explanation.surface: Someone refuses, for instance, to carry on after any alterations are made.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysay is a denial or refusal, the act of saying no.

clue.text: River joins ocean — payment demanded from one perching here

definitions.text: payment demanded from one perching here

blocks.note: the Trent, a major English river

explanation.surface: A river meets the sea, and someone resting there is charged for the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The river comes first in the clue but second in the answer, because it joins onto the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Seat rent is a charge for the use of a seat, as for a church pew or a deckchair where one sits.

clue.text: US lawman giving attention to president initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A US marshal listening closely to the President.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was the famous Wild West lawman of the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

clue.text: Orange colouring of pillar covering brown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom
the pillar wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: an anta is a pilaster at the end of a wall

explanation.surface: A column painted orange with a brown finish on top.
explanation.walkthrough: An anta is a classical architecture term, a square pilaster at the end of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatta, or annatto, is a red-orange dye from the seeds of a tropical tree, used to colour cheese.

clue.text: Food from cake shop cut the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means reading backwards

blocks.note: to cut someone is to snub them

explanation.surface: Pastries bought at a bakery have been sliced badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Buns are small sweet bread rolls of the kind sold in a bakery.

clue.text: Exuberant agent must snatch quick sleep

indicators.note: something snatched is held inside the grasp

explanation.surface: A lively secret agent has to grab forty winks.
explanation.definitionFit: Skippy means bouncy and playful, full of high spirits.

clue.text: Opposition with street being demolished, dwelling gone

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and taken away

explanation.surface: Protest when a street is torn down and homes disappear.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is taken out of RESISTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Resiance is an obsolete word for residence, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Child under sun sitting atop tree is rascal

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed under another comes after it
in a down entry, a piece sitting atop another is written before it

explanation.surface: A naughty child perched up a tree in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, positions like under and atop describe the order of pieces from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Schelm is an old word, from German, for a rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Little man cooks edible roots

blocks.note: to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A small chap prepares some root vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddoes are the starchy corms of taro, eaten as a vegetable in the tropics.

clue.text: Car hit by fly went in a bit of a circle

definitions.text: went in a bit of a circle

indicators.note: a vehicle that is hit is knocked out of shape

blocks.note: a ked is a wingless parasitic fly, the sheep tick

explanation.surface: A car is struck by an insect while it travels round a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcked is a variant past tense of arc, to move along a curved path that forms part of a circle.

clue.text: A British accountant's providing graphical representations

blocks.note: AC, short for accountant, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A British bookkeeper produces charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An abac is a nomogram, a chart from which values can be read off graphically.

clue.text: Cappuccino not half disgusting — so get this?

definitions.text: Cappuccino not half disgusting — so get this?

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word is thrown out
something disgusting is turned over and messed about

blocks.note: taken as written; its second half goes

explanation.surface: The coffee is half awful, so you might order something else instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: if the frothy coffee is nasty, have tea; CAPPU, the first half, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea, the obvious alternative to a bad coffee.

clue.text: Old women no longer advocates of revolution

blocks.note: first meaning: an archaic word for old women

explanation.surface: Elderly women who have stopped campaigning for an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot was once a term for an old woman, and Trots is the informal name for followers of Trotsky's permanent revolution.

clue.text: Sign of damage from wind — game restricted

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in by what surrounds it

blocks.note: the bise is a cold north wind in Switzerland and France

explanation.surface: Storm damage, and a match has to be curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The wind is an obscure regional one, and the game is the usual crossword abbreviation for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise is the discoloured mark left on skin or fruit by a blow.

clue.text: Announcer introducing goddess to lord

indicators.note: one piece is brought in ahead of the other

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies presents a goddess to a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald proclaims news or announces arrivals, so is an announcer.

clue.text: Language from some of those so thoughtful

indicators.note: only a portion of the following run of words is wanted

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken by certain very reflective people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesotho is the Bantu language of the Basotho people of Lesotho and South Africa.

clue.text: Bits of Italian food, cold, stimulated appetite, all except the first bit eaten

indicators.note: the opening letter has been consumed and so is gone
stimulated letters are stirred up into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, then losing its first letter

explanation.surface: Cold Italian food whets an appetite, and the whole lot is eaten but the first morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all' is a piece of the wordplay, not a general word; only its opening letter is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Cappelletti are small stuffed pasta shapes, little hats, from Italian cuisine.

clue.text: Old deer spits audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as it sounds when spoken out

blocks.note: a spit is a spade's depth of earth, so spits are spades

explanation.surface: An aged stag spitting noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A spayd is an obsolete term for a male red deer in its third year.

clue.text: In the main body find excellent African people

indicators.note: one piece is found in the middle of the other

blocks.note: the mass is the bulk or main body
A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Discovering a fine tribe in the heart of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, read as AI, is the standard crossword stand-in for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, pluralised here.
